Czech Epidemic Disrupts Economy as Lockdowns Hit Transport and Services

PRAGUE – Economic activity across the Czech Republic has slowed sharply as a new wave of the H7N3 influenza epidemic has prompted the government to impose strict lockdown measures. The nationwide restrictions, which include the closure of schools, non-essential shops, and a ban on public gatherings, have led to a significant reduction in mobility and consumer spending.

Public transport operators have been particularly hard-hit. Dopravni Podnik Hlm Prahy AS, the capital’s major public transit provider, reported a steep drop in ridership since the emergency measures came into force last week. “Passenger numbers on our metro, tram and bus services have fallen by over 60 percent compared to the same period last year,” said company spokesperson Jan Novak. “We are running reduced schedules and closely monitoring the situation, but the financial impact is already severe.”

Other sectors are feeling the strain as well. The Czech Confederation of Commerce and Tourism estimates that retail and hospitality revenues have declined by 45 percent on average since the start of the lockdown. “Many small businesses are at risk of closure if the restrictions continue into next month,” said confederation president Petra Cerná.

The government has pledged to provide support for affected firms, including wage subsidies and emergency grants, but business leaders warn that the measures may not be enough. “While we appreciate the government’s swift response, the current support package does not fully cover the fixed costs that many companies face during periods of zero revenue,” said Martin Chlada, chief economist at the financial consultancy Czechtek Advisors.

Analysts expect GDP growth forecasts for the second quarter to be revised downward if the lockdown persists. “The longer the epidemic disrupts normal life, the deeper the economic scars will be,” said Tomáš Brabenec, a senior economist at the Czech Economic Institute.

Health officials have not yet indicated when restrictions might be eased, as the number of confirmed H7N3 cases continues to climb. With the epidemic still under way and uncertainty lingering, businesses across the country are bracing for a protracted period of disruption.
